content: 1. Administration of fexinidazole may increase the risk of adverse effects associated with drugs that are substrates of the CYP3A4 enzyme. 2. Both fexinidazole and triclabendazole can prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative drugs. 3. Fexinidazole should not be coadministered with drugs that block potassium channels or prolong the QT interval. 4. Fexinidazole increases the levels or effects of trimethoprim by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 5. Fexinidazole inhibits the CYP3A4 enzyme, which may increase the risk of adverse effects when coadministered with CYP3A4 substrates. 6. Both fexinidazole and trimipramine prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 7. Fexinidazole increases the levels or effects of trimipramine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. At the maximum recommended dose, deutetrabenazine does not prolong the QT interval to a clinically relevant extent. Certain conditions may increase the risk of torsades de pointes or sudden death when associated with QTc-prolonging drugs (e.g., bradycardia, hypokalemia, hypomagnesemia, coadministration with other QTc-prolonging drugs, or congenital QT prolongation). 62. Due to the potential additive effect on heart rate, etrasimod may increase the risk of QT prolongation and torsades de pointes when coadministered with Class Ia or Class III antiarrhythmic drugs or other QT-prolonging drugs. 72.
